---
title: "Healthcare data analyst career evaluation"
subtitle: "Industry-label quality, market evidence and learning priorities"
---

## Research and product question

Which skills and work arrangements recur in US healthcare analyst postings, and how reliably can posting-derived features identify healthcare employers for reviewing that sample?

This project supports students targeting **healthcare data analyst roles in NAICS 62, Health Care and Social Assistance**. It adapts employer-industry classification research [@goindani2017] to a local Jobs_2026 snapshot [@jobs2026]. The observed sample supports an emphasis on SQL and visualization skills; sparse compensation evidence limits salary advice.

## Evidence at a glance

The January–September 2026 analysis selects **112 career postings** and a separate classification sample of **362 employers** from 2,350,355 source records. SQL appears in 63 career postings. Only three postings have a positive normalized salary with explicit USD. Employer-name-disjoint test F1 is 0.553 for linear SVM and 0.717 for GBDT, measuring agreement with dataset-derived labels.

## Submission boundaries

The structure follows the career evaluation pipeline in Module 1 [@ad688m1]. Sector 62 is broader than its preferred four- or six-digit scope. Personal skill assessments, team contribution and standup records, a final presentation, and public website deployment remain outstanding. The weighted opportunity scorecard is withheld because participant ratings and adequate salary coverage are unavailable. Completed classifier evaluation supplies the current substantial analytical component. These limitations should remain visible in any course submission.
